summary: Math.min selects the smallest numeric argument.
documentation: Math.min selects the smallest numeric argument. Comparing a request with a fixed upper bound implements a cap without sorting or changing the original value. With no arguments it returns Infinity; a NaN argument propagates NaN.
inputs: An object with requested and limit, both finite nonnegative numbers.
caution: This applies an upper bound only. Validate negative requests separately in a real ordering system.
scenarios: Cap a booking at the remaining seat count.
Limit a requested download batch to an API page limit.
Clamp a discount to its approved maximum.
title: Respect a request limit
problem: Input is {requested, limit}, both finite nonnegative numbers. Return the requested quantity capped at limit. Fractional quantities are allowed.
goal: Use Math.min() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Pass the request and limit as separate arguments.
